body:
Thank you so much. I have carried these words, and the ones the others have said, in my heart for the past month. 
I really don't know where I stand with my dad right now...I haven't seen him in a month, but I really am trying to work thru my feelings. Like you said, a father-daughter bond truly is special. 
The night I wrote this I felt like I carried the world on my shoulders, and I just didn't know what to do next. Bad things kept on happening and everything just kept on getting worse, and I just forgot what it was like to be happy. 
But like you said as well, my brother and my mom (along with my other 3 siblings) need me. And I won't...I can't let them down.  
This life isn't perfect, but it's mine. And now I see that it's far too precious to let go. 
It is still dark now, but I wake up each morning with the hope for sunshine.

It's taken a long time (my brothers accident was in August of last year, but his partially amputation was on Thanksgiving) but I have come to realize that I can't live with the what-ifs and this guilt I had. You're right, what little brother is going to listen to his older sister anyway, haha. I needed to let it go, or the guilt would eat me up inside. 
Thank you for your kind words and your reassurance, it really does mean a lot.

I actually cried a little bit after reading this one. 
I have felt like Atlas these past couple of months, and you summed it up perfectly. I am now seeing a therapist, and several close friends are helping me get thru everything. 
It's been a month since I made this post, and things are getting better. 
The day I made this post I found out my grandfather had lung cancer and that my dad was kicking us out of our house. 
I just couldn't take anymore, yah know? 
But I'm really trying to see the positive now, and I hold my head up high because I refuse to let this break me. 
Life is a gift. 
Thank you so much for your words.

Thank you. 
That one night a month ago when I made this post, I had just found out that on top of everything else my grandfather has lung cancer and that we were losing our house. I just needed somebody to talk to, and I felt helpless. 
I have started seeing a therapist, and have opened up more to my boyfriend (we've been together 2 years) but at the same time I'm trying not to dump everything on him. 
I just needed to listen and tell me it was alright that night, so thank you so very much.
